contentEn:
Homes built in British Columbia between 1978 and 1995 were frequently plumbed with Poly-B (cross-linked polyethylene) piping — a material that has aged poorly in Metro Vancouver's mineral-rich water supply. If your Burnaby bungalow, Richmond townhouse, or Coquitlam split-level was built during those years, your pipes may be approaching the end of their service life. Reno Stars has been replacing poly-b plumbing in Metro Vancouver homes since 2015, and this guide covers everything you need to know before you hire a contractor in 2026.

What Is Poly-B Piping and Why Is It a Problem?

Poly-B pipe is a flexible plastic tubing used for hot and cold water supply throughout millions of Canadian homes. It was favoured for its low material cost and ease of installation. However, the fittings — often made of brass — are the critical failure point. In Metro Vancouver's hard water conditions, mineral deposits accelerate corrosion inside those fittings, leading to micro-fractures, joint failures, and water leaks that can go undetected behind walls for months.

The tell-tale signs that you have Poly-B plumbing include:

  • Intermittent water discolouration (brown or yellow tint)
  • Low water pressure at individual fixtures
  • Visible oxidation or green crusting on brass fittings under sinks
  • A home inspection report noting "Poly-B" or "cross-linked polyethylene" supply piping

How Much Does Poly-B Pipe Replacement Cost in Vancouver in 2026?

The total cost to replace Poly-B piping in a typical Greater Vancouver single-family home ranges from $3,000 to $15,000, depending on the size of the home, the configuration of the existing plumbing, and whether the work involves opening finished walls. These are the figures our project teams quote most frequently:

  • Repiping a 1970s-1980s Vancouver Special (1,200-1,500 sq ft): $3,500 - $6,000
  • Repiping a 1990s Richmond townhouse (1,500-2,000 sq ft): $5,000 - $9,000
  • Full repipe of a 1985 Coquitlam single-family home (2,000-2,500 sq ft): $8,000 - $15,000

Costs include demolition of drywall to access pipes, installation of new copper or PEX tubing, pressure testing, and professional patching and repainting. Reno Stars provides a fixed-price quote after an in-home inspection, so there are no surprises once work begins.

Does Home Insurance Cover Poly-B Replacement?

Many BC home insurers have updated their policies regarding Poly-B plumbing. Some underwriters now require a plumbing assessment as a condition of renewal, and a growing number refuse to insure homes with documented Poly-B piping at any price. Others will cover the home but may exclude water damage arising from Poly-B failure — meaning a burst pipe claim could be denied.

Before starting work, contact your insurance provider and ask two specific questions: Does my policy cover water damage from Poly-B pipe failure? Will replacing the pipes improve my insurability or premium? Getting the answers in writing protects you if a dispute arises later.

What Material Replaces Poly-B?

Modern replacement piping in BC typically uses one of two materials:

  • PEX (cross-linked polyethylene): Flexible, freeze-resistant, and approved by the BC Building Code. PEX tubing connects with crimp or expansion fittings and carries a 25-year manufacturer warranty.
  • Copper: Rigid, long-lasting (50+ year lifespan), and preferred in high-rise buildings where aesthetics permit exposed runs. Copper is more labour-intensive to install but remains the premium choice for whole-home repiping.

Most Reno Stars projects use PEX for its balance of cost, durability, and BC Building Code compliance. Your estimator will recommend the right solution for your home's configuration on the day of inspection.

How Long Does Poly-B Repiping Take?

For a typical Greater Vancouver single-family home, the physical repiping work takes 3 to 7 working days. This includes wall opening, pipe replacement, pressure testing with a licensed plumber, and coordination with a drywall contractor for patching and painting. Finishing work (texturing, painting, trim) may add another 3 to 5 days depending on contractor availability.

Reno Stars manages the full trade sequence in-house — plumbing, drywall, painting, and final inspection — so homeowners deal with one project manager from start to finish rather than coordinating multiple subcontractors.

Planning a renovation in Metro Vancouver? Reno Stars offers free, no-obligation quotes for whole-home repiping and all major renovation projects. Contact us online or call our Burnaby office to schedule an inspection.

Frequently Asked Questions

How do I know if my Vancouver home has Poly-B piping?

Look for grey or blue-grey plastic tubing (sometimes white or black) with brass fittings at connection points. Poly-B is most commonly found in homes built between 1978 and 1995. A home inspection report will confirm the material, or a licensed plumber can identify it during a visual inspection.

Can I just replace the fittings instead of repiping the whole house?

Partial repairs are sometimes possible when the pipe itself is in good condition and the failure is limited to specific fittings. However, if your home is over 25 years old with Poly-B, a full repipe is almost always more cost-effective in the long run — partial repairs frequently reveal additional compromised joints once work begins.

Does the BC Building Code require me to replace Poly-B piping?

The BC Building Code does not mandate replacement of existing Poly-B piping in good condition. However, if you are renovating a bathroom or kitchen and the walls are already open, replacing accessible poly-b sections is strongly recommended by building inspectors and is considered a best practice by licensed plumbing contractors.

Does Reno Stars handle the permits for poly-b repiping in Vancouver?

Yes. Reno Stars obtains all required plumbing permits from the City of Vancouver, City of Burnaby, City of Richmond, or the applicable municipality before starting work. We also coordinate the mandatory final plumbing inspection and provide homeowners with documentation for insurance purposes.
contentZh:
卑诗省于1978年至1995年间建造的大量住宅使用了Poly-B（交联聚乙烯）管道——一种在温哥华含矿物质丰富的水质条件下老化严重的水管材料。如果您的本拿比平房、列治文联排别墅或高贵林错层式住宅建于那些年份，您家中的管道可能已接近使用寿命的尾声。Reno Stars自2015年以来一直在为大温地区的房屋更换Poly-B管道，本指南涵盖您在2026年聘请承包商前需要了解的所有信息。

什么是Poly-B管道，为什么它是个问题？

Poly-B管道是一种柔性塑料管，用于整个加拿大数百万住宅的冷热水供应。它因材料成本低，安装方便而受到青睐。然而，问题出在连接件——通常由黄铜制成——这是关键故障点。在大温哥华地区的硬水条件下，矿物质沉积加速了这些连接件内部的腐蚀，导致微裂纹、接头故障和漏水，而这些漏水可能在墙壁后面潜伏数月不被发现。

判断您家中是否有Poly-B管道的明显迹象包括：

  • 间歇性水质变色（棕色或黄色）
  • 个别用水点水压低
  • 水槽下方黄铜连接件可见氧化或绿色水垢
  • 验房报告中注明"Poly-B"或"交联聚乙烯"供水管道

2026年温哥华Poly-B管道更换费用是多少？

在大温哥华典型独立住宅中更换Poly-B管道的总费用约为3,000至15,000加元，具体取决于房屋大小、现有管道配置以及是否需要打开已装修的墙壁。以下是我们项目团队最常引用的数据：

  • 更换1970-80年代温哥华特色住宅（1,200-1,500平方英尺）：$3,500 - $6,000
  • 更换1990年代列治文联排别墅（1,500-2,000平方英尺）：$5,000 - $9,000
  • 全面更换1985年高贵林独立住宅（2,000-2,500平方英尺）：$8,000 - $15,000

费用包括拆除干墙以进入管道、安装新的铜管或PEX管道、压力测试以及专业修补和粉刷。Reno Stars在上门勘察后提供固定价格报价，因此开工后不会有任何意外。

房屋保险是否涵盖Poly-B更换？

许多卑诗省的房屋保险公司已更新了关于Poly-B管道的政策。一些承保人现在要求将管道评估作为续保条件，越来越多承保人拒绝为有记录显示使用Poly-B管道的房屋提供保险——无论价格多少。其他公司可能会承保房屋本身，但可能排除Poly-B故障造成的水损——这意味着爆管索赔可能会被拒绝。

在开始工作之前，请联系您的保险提供商并询问两个具体问题：我的保单是否涵盖Poly-B管道故障造成的水损？更换管道会改善我的承保范围或保费吗？以书面形式获取答案可以在日后发生纠纷时保护您。

用什么材料替代Poly-B？

卑诗省现代更换管道通常使用两种材料之一：

  • PEX（交联聚乙烯)：柔性、耐冻、获卑诗省建筑规范批准。PEX管道通过压接或扩张接头连接，享有25年制造商保修。
  • 铜管：刚性、耐久（50年以上使用寿命)，在允许明装的高层建筑中是首选。铜管安装人工成本更高，但仍是全屋管道更换的优质选择。

Reno Stars大多数项目使用PEX，因其性价比高、耐用且符合卑诗省建筑规范。您的估算师将在勘察当天为您的房屋布局推荐正确的解决方案。

Poly-B管道更换需要多长时间？

对于典型的大温哥华独立住宅，管道更换的实际施工时间为3至7个工作日。这包括墙壁开凿、管道更换、由持牌水管工进行压力测试，以及与干墙承包商协调修补和粉刷。收尾工作（纹理处理、粉刷、装饰条）根据承包商可用性可能再增加3至5天。

Reno Stars内部管理全套工序——管道，干墙、粉刷和最终检查——因此业主从始至终只与一位项目经理对接，而无需协调多个分包商。

计划在大温哥华进行装修？Reno Stars为全屋管道更换及所有主要装修项目提供免费、无义务报价。在线联系我们或致电我们的本拿比办公室预约勘察。

常见问题

如何知道我的温哥华住宅是否有Poly-B管道？

寻找灰色或蓝灰色塑料管（有时为白色或黑色)，连接点有黄铜配件。Poly-B最常见于1978年至1995年间建造的房屋。验房报告将确认材料类型，或持牌水管工可在目视检查期间识别。

我是否可以只更换配件而不更换整栋房子的管道？

当管道本身状况良好且故障仅限于特定配件时，局部维修有时是可行的。但是，如果您的房屋使用Poly-B且超过25年房龄，全屋更换几乎总是长期来看更具成本效益——局部维修一旦开工经常会发现其他受损接头。

卑诗省建筑规范是否要求我更换Poly-B管道？

卑诗省建筑规范不要求更换状况良好的现有Poly-B管道。但是，如果您正在装修浴室或厨房且墙壁已经打开，打开通道更换可触及的Poly-B管道段是建筑检查员强烈建议的，也是持牌水管承包商公认的最佳实践。

Reno Stars是否为温哥华的Poly-B管道更换处理许可证？

是的。Reno Stars在开工前向温哥华市、本拿比市、列治文市或适用 municipality 申请所有必需的管道许可证。我们还协调强制性的最终管道检查，并为业主提供保险文档。
